Other than that, I'm interested in notifications, of course, and calendar views. Voice calling/texting isn't a huge concern, though. When I need to voice dial, I'm usually in my car and use the car's Bluetooth connection. Battery life is pretty important- I don't want to charge every night.

I've been looking at a Pebble Time Steel, but they aren't out yet- at least AFAIK. Also an LG Urbane. Any thoughts, advice, or additional recommendations?

As far as I'm aware, OG pebble and OG pebble steel are the only smartwatches that aren't that brilliant with fitness tracking. The main limiting factor for you is going to have to be battery life. Most of these watches really don't have the best battery life. I've been able to get by 2-3 days on my urbane with the always on feature on but pretty much everything else disabled and on average screen brightness. Urbane looks a lot better both by screen and looks than the OG steel I had and the reviews of the Time's display didn't give me great hope in going for it which is why I decided to give an Android Wear device a shot. All in all having had the opportunity to get a bit of hands on experience and in doing some personal research of my own I'd say if you are going for features then smartwatches and fitness trackers are actually quite generic, they display similar results in slightly different way. There's a bit more differentiation with battery life between brands' current lineup but not much, I'm fairly certain I could get fairly similar life out of the Gear or the 360 as I do with the Urbane (Just like everything else, the actual battery life depends on how heavily you use it). All I can recommend is trying to avoid the Apple watch. As far as I can tell, it is designed to be a flashy pretty piece of jewelry which can only mean that it must also be a very thirsty machine. Smartwatches' main competition is in it's looks, just like most of your regular old watches. If you're utilitarian and really don't care about looks then you're pretty much sorted and could save a couple hundred and get a smartwatch with all the features of even the most expensive smartwatches, otherwise you spend some more for something flashier and prettier. Urbane looks and feels just like your average large watch you'd get from the jewelry case at some retail location and I like it for that (Huawei watch has a similar design). Many smartwatch makers try for an individualized personal design which, contrary to rightnowscow's opinion, I don't think are exactly dorky but rather add a unique and maybe a bit provocative flair of personality. Who knows, maybe it'll give some inspiration to shake up the wardrobe a bit.

TL;DR - If you're looking for a device that will give you notifications, personal events, and fitness tracking, even the crappiest smartwatch can do that reliably. Battery life can be broken into 3 categories: Pebble=stellar (OG steel had no problems w/ 5-7 days), Apple=poor (BARRRELY survives long enough to be put back on the charger when going to bed), Everything else=mediocre (Urbane I've managed 2-3 days w/ minimal usage + Always On.
